Technology stocks still were higher in late trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding almost 0.9% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising over 1.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Sparton ( SPA ) was more than 1% lower shortly before Monday's closing bell, reversing an over 1% rise for the electronic components company that followed it saying its ERAPSCO joint venture with Ultra Electronics Holdings plc has won a $64.6 million subcontract to manufacture sonobuoys for the U.S. Navy. The project is expected to be completed by April 2020.
In other sector news:
+ Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) jumped out to a 12-year high on Monday after the chipmaker said it has introduced the Radeon Pro V340 graphics card, a high-performance dual-GPU virtual desktop infrastructure device. The AMD Radeon Pro V340 graphics card is expected to be available during Q4.
- VMware ( VMW ) has turned lower Monday afternoon, sinking almost 1%, after activist investors Elliott Management reportedly voiced its opposition to a bid by Dell Technologies' ( DVMT ) attempt to buy the tracking stock tied to its interest in VMWare ( VMW ) for $22 billion. "They made it clear they are against it," an unnamed source who spoke directly to Elliott a few weeks ago told the New York Post while another source said the hedge fund believes certain aspects of the deal are "pretty awful."
FuelCell Energy ( FCEL ) fell over 6% on Monday after pricing a nearly $27 million offering of 30,680 shares of its Series D convertible preferred stock at $880.0522 per share. The preferred shares are convertible into FuelCell common stock at $1.38 per share, representing a 20% premium over its Aug. 24 closing price of $1.15 a share. Net proceeds will be used for working capital, project financing, and general corporate purposes.
